title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 295
paragraphs: In one respect the Egyptians agree with some of the Hellenes — namely, with the Lacedaemonians, but not with the rest: that is, their younger men, when they meet their elders, give way and move out of the path; and when their elders approach, they rise from their seats. In the following, however, they do not agree with any of the Hellenes: instead of addressing one another on the roads, they do reverence, lowering the hand down to the knee.
